name: Leisach
kurzbeschreibung: Village at the entrance of the Iseltal valley, featuring an Erlebnisbad (experience bath) and stunning views of the Lienzer Dolomiten.
beschreibung:
Overview

Leisach is a historic mountain municipality in East Tyrol within the Lienz district, situated at an altitude of 712 metres at the western gateway to the Lienz basin. Home to approximately 900 residents, the community nestles against the dramatic limestone base of the Lienz Dolomites, overshadowed by the towering rock monolith of Mount Spitzkofel (2,717 m). Positioned at the geographical convergence between the Puster Valley and the Drau Valley at the bottleneck of the Lienzer Klause gorge, Leisach is widely regarded as the historic "Gateway to Lienz". Featuring an eventful military past, intact mountain farming hamlets, a charming forest swimming pool, and direct access to alpine treks, the village blends history with alpine adventure.

History

The strategic bottleneck of the Lienzer Klause elevated Leisach to a critical defensive position as early as ancient times. The village first appeared in historical documents in 1060 under the Slavic name Lyzach. During the late Middle Ages, the Counts of Gorizia erected the commanding fortress of the Lienzer Klause to seal off access to the Puster Valley against hostile incursions. The fortress achieved heroic status during the Tyrolean Rebellion of August 1809, when local East Tyrolean riflemen successfully ambushed and repelled advancing Napoleonic forces in a fierce battle. The parish church of Saint Michael, displaying neo-Gothic interiors alongside an authentic late-Gothic bell tower, remains the spiritual core of the village.

Getting There

Leisach benefits from outstanding transport connectivity. Motorists travel west from Lienz along the B100 Drautal road towards South Tyrol, reaching the municipality in just a few minutes. Travelers arriving from Carinthia continue westward through Lienz along the B100, while those arriving from South Tyrol and Italy follow the Pustertal road past Innichen and Sillian directly into Leisach. Rail travelers can alight at Lienz main station, where frequent local buses operated by the Tyrol Public Transport Network connect directly to Leisach. The celebrated Drau Cycle Path (R1) also passes directly through the village.

Tips

A tour of the historic Lienzer Klause fortress offers thrilling insights into the Tyrolean liberation battles of 1809 and medieval defensive fortifications. On warm summer afternoons, the picturesque Leisach Forest Pool, set within pine woods and featuring solar-heated waters and relaxing lawns, is a favourite retreat for families. Mountaineers will relish hiking up the untamed Kerschbaumertal valley via the Kerschbaumeralm to the Lienz Dolomites Mountain Refuge at 1,974 metres, surrounded by towering limestone spires. Cyclists can enjoy a leisurely, level ride along the Drau Cycle Path into nearby Lienz.
